title: Latin numbers
description: The months counted in Latin, from Primus to Tertius Decimus, the way the Romans counted theirs
origin: These names are a modern invention: Latin ordinal numbers, first to thirteenth, in the masculine to agree with mensis, month, as Roman month names did. The Romans counted months the same way: their year began in March, which is why September, October, November and December mean seventh, eighth, ninth and tenth. This calendar also starts in March, so Septimus to Decimus land almost exactly on September to December.
pronunciation: Classical Latin as scholars reconstruct it, with hard c and g, v as w, and long vowels held longer. These are well-attested Latin numbers, so we are quite sure of them. Church Latin and English-style Latin sound different.

leapWeek.name: Leap week
leapWeek.meaning: A spare week after Tertius Decimus, about one year in six, which keeps the count in step with the equinox.

months.name: Primus
months.meaning: Latin for first. Like the early Roman year, this calendar begins in March.

months.name: Quintus
months.meaning: Latin for fifth. The Romans called the fifth month Quintilis, which later became July.

months.name: Sextus
months.meaning: Latin for sixth. The Romans called the sixth month Sextilis, which later became August.

months.name: Septimus
months.meaning: Latin for seventh, as in September, the seventh month of the March-based Roman year.
months.notes: Runs 7 Sep to 4 Oct in 2026, almost exactly September.

months.name: Octavus
months.meaning: Latin for eighth, as in October.

months.name: Nonus
months.meaning: Latin for ninth, as in November. The Roman nones, a day in each month, got their name from the same word.

months.name: Decimus
months.meaning: Latin for tenth, as in December. It holds the December solstice.

months.name: Undecimus
months.meaning: Latin for eleventh. In the March-based Roman year, January was the eleventh month.

months.name: Duodecimus
months.meaning: Latin for twelfth. In the March-based Roman year, February was the twelfth and last month.

months.name: Tertius Decimus
months.meaning: Latin for thirteenth, literally third and tenth, the form classical writers used.
